applied_additions.summary: <certain> Keep canonical JSON + SHA-256 for the continuity record. The unmet half of ADR-004 is the readable projection, so fix the projection rather than revisit the format.
<certain> CheckpointIntent is the only agent-facing writer view. commit stays host-side for compaction proofs. This honours the writer-view ADR instead of collapsing the two commands.

<certain> Standardize bundle verbs: validate (schema-only dry-run), schema <name> (catalog JSON Schema), lint (store integrity), handoff (replaces handoff-cli). Drop the -cli suffix repo-wide in its own PR.

<certain> Apply schema simplifications S2-S8 as listed in working_context, with S6 strictness first. The kernel guarantees (derived status, transitions with rationale, immutable receipts, digests, compaction proofs) are kept unchanged.
<certain> Human view is the projection: add a body (notes, entries with summaries, context, links, dossier as Markdown), plus list and log commands. Double down here before the SKILL.md rewrite.
<speculating> Exclude wheypoint from the #553 grounding metric; it writes checkpoints and makes no decisions. User has not confirmed.

Should an active question default to blocks_continuation=true, or should the projection surface open non-gating entries so a human can tell ok-with-open-questions from ok? Today three open questions render as status ok with 'Gating entries: none'.
Catalog registration: move the wheypoint types into contracts.py, or teach the @contract scan to walk a module list? The scan reads only contracts.py globals today.
Does commit stay a public command for compaction proofs, or does checkpoint grow a --compacted path that takes the proof block? Either keeps the proof caller-authored.
